In a recent development, our product picks are editor-tested, expert-approved. We may earn a commission through links on our site. Why Trust Us?

Recent findings suggest that TODD SNYDER makes some of our favorite menswear, and for its latest collaboration, the Latest York brand crossed the pond to Scotland. The draw? Lagavulin, the distillery that’s been making smoky Scotch whisky on the island of Islay for more than 200 years.

Sources indicate that the partnership marks Snyder’s 15th anniversary, with clothes that borrow from Islay’s rugged landscape. Standouts include a brown suede jacket lined in Lagavulin’s own tartan and Fair Isle zip-ups in the earthy shades of the Scottish moors. Pretty great reasons to look forward to sweater weather.

Fronting the campaign is Ben Ahlers. As footman-turned-businessman Jack Trotter on The Gilded Age, the 30-year-old actor knows his way around heritage menswear. Still, these relaxed layers are pretty easy to picture on the streets of Newly introduced York. We caught up with him about what playing Jack taught him about getting dressed—and which piece he’d bring home.

MEN’S HEALTH: You spend a lot of time in period costumes on The Gilded Age. Has anything from Jack’s wardrobe made its way into how you dress off-screen?

It has been revealed that BEN AHLERS: Jack has a consistency to the way that he dresses. As a footman, he had a uniform, and as a young businessman, he has a pretty steady throughline through his looks—a base structure with really well-made clothing and then accents like a tie or a tie pin or a ring that can allow for a sense of creative expression. I find that I like a level of consistency in my own personal dress as well.

More than anything, the greatest benefit of living inside of the clothing that Kasia [Walicka Maimone, the show’s costume designer] and her incredible team make for us every year is this awareness of the way clothes not only make you present to the world but also how they make you feel within them.

MH: Is there a menswear trend from that era you wish more guys would embrace today?

Sources indicate that BA: I would love to see some of the creativity come out in menswear and in the accent work, like a tie pin. Some of the tie pins we have on this show are just so well-crafted and specific. The heads of canes the men wore back then also have such an artistry to them, and there aren’t a lot of avenues for that sort of expression in modern menswear. It’d be nice to see that creative voice or risk-taking come through in the subtle accents that we wear in our day-to-day life.

MH: Your role in Death of a Salesman got people talking about your physique. How did you prepare?

BA: For Death of a Salesman, I knew earlier on in the development process that they wanted to go the direction that they did for the top of the show, and so I knew that I was going to be kind of exposed every night. I really tried to go to the gym during the rehearsal process because I knew once we opened the show that it was going to be hard to stay as active—the show was just so draining.

The couple of months up to opening, I really made a practice of five days a week of cross-training, lifting, running, and yoga, and trying to keep my body as nimble and buoyant as possible, because the subject matter and the daily grind of showing up to the theater every day can really take a toll.

Sources indicate that during the run, a lot of my focus was on rest, recovery, sauna, cold plunge, diet, stretching, because I’d already built the foundation of the physicality. Throughout the five-month run, it came down to being sure that I was healthy and recovering as best as I could.

MH: What happened between takes on the Todd Snyder shoot that we’d never know from looking at the campaign photos?

Sources indicate that BA: Between takes, I had a blast with Boo George, our photographer. He is such a character and one of the best energies on set, and really delivered in the work. The whole crew from Todd Snyder and Lagavulin were so supportive, and it was such a fun little escape for all of us to exist on this island in the most beautiful landscape imaginable.

Sources indicate that I really enjoyed getting to know a lot of the locals there. Many of the people there worked at the distillery, and I got to see firsthand how the whisky was actually made. People were so proud to share their culture as well as their craft with the world.

MH: Which piece from the collection would you wear back home in Newly introduced York, and what would you pair it with?

Recent findings suggest that BA: My favorite piece from the collection is the Todd Snyder x Lagavulin suede stable jacket, inspired by the texture and color of the mossy peat that coats Islay. It’s a perfect fall jacket, and I’d pair it with Todd Snyder’s relaxed barrel jean in khaki, which I think would really pop.

In Dogecoin ecosystem news, DogeOS is nearing mainnet launch, bringing an EVM-compatible app layer to DOGE that would let developers build DeFi, games and other apps on Dogecoin for the first time.

In October, DogeOS opened a public test network for Ethereum-style trading, lending and other applications using DOGE, seeking to give Dogecoin holders more ways to use their coins beyond payments and price speculation.

In a recent post on X, Dogecoin Foundation director of product Timothy Stebbing shared a Dogecoin ecosystem 2026 revision.

Stebbing predicts that the next three to four years for Dogecoin are likely to be shaped more by the development and adoption of smart-contract application layers than by large, pre-emptive changes to Dogecoin’s base protocol. He cited DogeOS as an early and visible example of that direction. If it and similar efforts succeed in attracting sustained developer activity and real usage while continuing to treat Dogecoin as the settlement and value-transfer foundation, Stebbing sees the ecosystem gaining additional utility without compromising the simplicity and reliability of the Layer 1.

However, the proposed mechanism for native proof verification on Dogecoin still requires community discussion and, ultimately, activation. Thus, adoption will depend on whether the resulting applications are useful enough that people choose to use them. None of these uncertainties change the underlying architectural advantage: the Layer 1 can remain a focused means of exchange while the surrounding ecosystem gains the capacity for richer functionality.

#6099. Industry News: 4 named oceans, 1 body of water: what the Atlantic, Pacific, Indian and Arctic stand for

📅 16 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 7m • 📚 Deep Dive (1470 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Qz ↗ Open Full Page

Industry News: 4 named oceans, 1 body of water: what the Atlantic, Pacific, Indian and Arctic stand for

📅 16 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1470 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Qz

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that NOAA claims Earth has one global ocean covering 71 percent of the planet.
  • Most people learned the oceans from a classroom globe, where names such as Pacific and Atlantic sit in different places as if each were its own body of water.
  • Industry observers note that even the number of oceans is not fixed, and it moves between four and five depending on a single decision about borders.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that NOAA claims Earth has one global ocean covering 71 percent of the planet. See what 4 of its named regions stand for.

Most people learned the oceans from a classroom globe, where names such as Pacific and Atlantic sit in different places as if each were its own body of water. The water on that globe is one connected ocean. The familiar names mark regions of that single ocean. They do not mark separate oceans. The count of oceans therefore depends on where people decide one region stops and the next begins.

Industry observers note that even the number of oceans is not fixed, and it moves between four and five depending on a single decision about borders. NOAA counts the Southern Ocean as a basin of its own when it compares the oceans by size. One common definition places it everywhere south of 60° S, according to Britannica. The fifth ocean is a line of latitude that mapmakers drew around Antarctica, and the water inside it is the same water as before. If drawing one line can add an ocean, then drawing other lines can make the oceans already named larger or smaller. That happens region by region, and by very different amounts.

The NOAA National Ocean Service set out to count how many named oceans exist and what they are, including the Pacific, the Atlantic and the Arctic. The agency that set out to count the oceans concluded that there is really only one to count. "There is only one global ocean," the NOAA National Ocean Service noted. Of Earth's entire surface, 71 percent lies under that single ocean. Each named ocean is a convention people laid over that water, so the count is a count of names. Yet the names are not interchangeable. The regions they mark differ enormously in size and depth, in how well people know them, and in what they mean for people living on land. Each name stands for something different. One is a region whose size depends on where its borders fall. Another is the largest region, and earthquakes and volcanoes ring it. A third is a region tied to the rains of South and Southeast Asia. The last is a frozen region full of life.

The Atlantic is one of the oceans people know best, but it is not the biggest. The NOAA National Ocean Service counts it among the four historically named oceans and among the three best known. The Atlantic is still second in both area and volume, according to Britannica. Second place is a vast expanse, and the 85.133 million square kilometers most people would accept as the Atlantic's size looks exact and fixed. That figure holds only as long as everyone agrees on where the Atlantic ends.

Industry observers note that the Atlantic has the least settled borders of the significant oceans, even though its name is one of the oldest and most familiar on any map. "The Atlantic exhibits the largest change in surface area and volume when its marginal seas are subtracted," Alyn C. Duxbury, a research associate professor emeritus of oceanography at the University of Washington, Seattle, remarked, as reported by Britannica. The question of how big the Atlantic is therefore has no single answer. The answer depends on whether the bays and seas along its edges count as part of it. Even an ocean whose existence no one disputes has a size that comes partly from where people draw its boundaries.

The Atlantic's edges affect its depth as well as its area. Its surface is larger than the Indian Ocean's 70.560 million square kilometers, yet the Atlantic is on average 3,646 meters deep, compared with 3,741 meters for the Indian Ocean, according to Britannica. An ocean that is large but relatively shallow fits a size that rests partly on shallow bordering seas, though the depth figures alone don't prove it.

The Atlantic outranks the Indian Ocean in surface area, but its water does not reach as far down on average.

Recent findings suggest that the Pacific Ocean is one of the four historically named oceans and among the three best known, according to the NOAA National Ocean Service. Calling it familiar undersells it, because the Pacific covers 168.723 million square kilometers of the planet's surface, according to Britannica. A globe that prints each ocean's name in the same type suggests a set of rough equals. Anyone who pictures the oceans that way is picturing the labels on the map, not the water beneath them.

Industry observers note that the Pacific is as deep as it is wide. NOAA reports that it is the deepest ocean basin, and that depth does not rest on one famous trench. Its floor lies an average of 3,970 meters down, according to Britannica, so great depth is the ordinary condition across the whole basin rather than a record set in a single spot. The Pacific's lead comes from depth as well as surface, and it amounts to more than the biggest patch of blue on a globe.

The Pacific's edges deserve as much attention as its size. The Pacific basin is known as the Ring of Fire, NOAA reports, and the name comes from the volcanoes and earthquakes clustered around its edges. People who live along the Pacific's borders have a reason to care about them that goes beyond distance or trade. For them, the edge of this ocean is a source of danger.

The largest region of the one ocean is also the one with a ring of volcanoes along its border, and its size tells only half of its story.

People know the Indian Ocean for its history and its weather, not for its size. On a globe it sits among the big familiar names as if it were their equal. It is one of the four historically named oceans and among the three best known, according to the NOAA National Ocean Service. NOAA ranks it as only the third-largest ocean basin, which makes it the smallest of the three oceans most people can name. Its place among them must rest on something other than how much water it holds, and that something is what people have done on it and what it does for people on land.

People learned the Indian Ocean's name early because they sailed it early. It was the first ocean that people navigated extensively, according to Encyclopedia.com. It became a working sea rather than an empty space at the edge of a chart, and its name stands for a sea route as much as for a basin.

According to recent reports, people who live far from the Indian Ocean's coasts also depend on its weather. Its monsoons are the source of heavy rainfall in western India and Southeast Asia, according to Encyclopedia.com, so the wet season in those regions has its origin over this ocean. The connection also runs from land to sea. The Ganges, the Indus and the Brahmaputra are among the sources of the ocean's sediment, which ties the Indian Ocean to the great river systems of South Asia.

Of the familiar ocean names, this one says the least about size and the most about how closely people on shore live with a stretch of water.

Sources indicate that the Arctic shares the old title of ocean with three far better-known regions, yet it is the smallest and least familiar of them all. It is less commonly known than the Atlantic, Pacific and Indian oceans, according to the NOAA National Ocean Service, and NOAA ranks it the smallest of the five ocean basins. That ranking puts the Arctic below even the Southern Ocean, the basin that mapmakers created by drawing a line around Antarctica. The least-known ocean still lies at the top of very familiar maps, with Alaska, Canada, Greenland, Norway and Russia all facing it along their northern coasts, according to NOAA. Its small size and low profile say little about how much life the region holds.

The Arctic's sea ice is a home for living things, not a bare white surface over empty water. Many people picture the top of the globe as frozen and lifeless. Bacteria and algae live inside the brine channels that run through the sea ice, NOAA reports, which places life inside the ice at the bottom of the food chain. Polar bears live on that same ice, so the frozen surface supports animals as large as bears as well as organisms too small to see. That makes the region a working ecosystem rather than an empty stretch of white.

In this smallest region of the one ocean, the frozen surface is itself the habitat, and any loss of ice would leave less room for the algae inside it and the bears on top of it.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • by Todd Bishop & John Cook on Nov 14, 2026 at 2:10 pmNovember 14, 2026 at 2:10 pm.
  • It has been revealed that nvidia’s board says it’s too early to speculate about who will succeed Jensen Huang.
  • Sources indicate that the board noted in a statement Friday that it’s still choosing a search firm and hasn’t formally engaged any candidates.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

by Todd Bishop & John Cook on Nov 14, 2026 at 2:10 pmNovember 14, 2026 at 2:10 pm.

It has been revealed that nvidia’s board says it’s too early to speculate about who will succeed Jensen Huang. Sorry, we’re having too much fun coming up with names.

Sources indicate that the board noted in a statement Friday that it’s still choosing a search firm and hasn’t formally engaged any candidates. That came after the Financial Times reported that the board had approached Arm CEO Rene Haas — a name John had presciently floated when we recorded this week’s GeekWire Podcast on Thursday.

Nvidia declared Huang’s resignation Thursday, a day after the Latest York Times reported that he’d had an affair with an Nvidia executive who reported to him. Days earlier, he admitted to an affair with a woman U.S. intelligence officials reportedly suspected of being a Chinese spy.

In a recent development, colette Kress, the organization’s longtime CFO, is serving as interim CEO. She spent 13 years at Microsoft earlier in her career.

Others would rather have Huang back.

Two major Nvidia investors, Altimeter Capital’s Brad Gerstner and Atreides Management’s Gavin Baker, asked the board to run a deliberate search that leaves open “the potential return of Jensen Huang.” Elon Musk stated on X that he was signing a petition to reinstate Huang.

The organizers of one, called “Stand with Jensen,” say it has more than 108,000 names, including more than 5,600 people who identify themselves as current Nvidia employees.

It has been revealed that the case for Haas: The Arm CEO spent about seven years at Nvidia, rising to vice president and general manager of its computing products business, before joining Arm in 2013. He became Arm’s CEO in February 2022, when Nvidia’s $40 billion deal to acquire Arm collapsed amid regulatory opposition. SoftBank, Arm’s majority owner, kept Nvidia’s $1.25 billion prepayment.

According to recent reports, arm, based in Cambridge, England, designs processor technology that’s ubiquitous in smartphones, and licenses it to other chipmakers. That includes Nvidia, whose Grace data center CPU, paired with its GPUs in AI systems, is built on Arm cores. Amazon’s Graviton and Microsoft’s Cobalt server chips also use Arm designs.

Haas is one of several candidates, and there’s no guarantee he’ll be offered the job or take it, the FT reported.

It has been revealed that he also has a link to Harvey Jones, the longtime Nvidia director named the organization’s first board chair this week. Haas was vice president of sales at Tensilica, a chip-design company, from 1999 to 2004, according to his LinkedIn profile. Jones co-founded Tensilica and chaired its board until chip-design software maker Cadence acquired it in 2013.

Haas has also seen Huang’s resistance to succession planning firsthand. “He didn’t like the idea,” Haas mentioned in a 2024 interview, as quoted by the New York Times this week. “He felt it would create competition among executives and be divisive.”.

One complication: SoftBank named Haas CEO of SoftBank Group International in April, helping coordinate chip and AI companies in its international portfolio while he continues to run Arm. The FT reported that the appointment was aimed at pushing forward Project Izanagi, SoftBank’s AI chip effort launched to compete with Nvidia.

He knows Nvidia from the inside, but he also knows what it’s like to run a public company — which matters for a board searching in the middle of a crisis.

John’s argument on the podcast: Nvidia needs someone who can shepherd a company through turmoil, not just a great technologist. Think Alan Mulally going from Boeing to Ford, or Dara Khosrowshahi moving from Expedia to Uber after Travis Kalanick’s ouster.

What the betting markets say: On Kalshi, Ian Buck, the Nvidia vice president who created the CUDA software platform, was the favorite at midday Friday. By midday Saturday, Haas had overtaken him, at 25% to Buck’s 18%. Kress was at 10%.

The Axios list of 11 names also includes Apple Executive Chair Tim Cook, for whom President Trump lobbied on Truth Social (“A Legend replaces a Legend!”), along with AMD CEO Lisa Su and Google Cloud CEO Thomas Kurian.

In a recent development, A Northwest wildcard: Analysts have also floated Sanjay Mehrotra, CEO of Boise, Idaho-based Micron Technology, whose memory chips power Nvidia’s AI servers. Mehrotra co-founded SanDisk in 1988 and has run Micron since 2017.

The AWS chief: Matt Garman has run Amazon Web Services since June 2024, overseeing a business with a $142 billion annual revenue run rate at the end of last year. He started at Amazon as an MBA intern in 2005, joined AWS full time in 2006 as one of its first product managers, and later led its compute business and then its sales and marketing organization.

Another Amazon pick: We’d also look at Peter DeSantis, who now leads a new organization that includes Amazon’s AI models, custom chips and quantum computing, reporting directly to CEO Andy Jassy.

DeSantis joined Amazon as a software developer in 1998. He led the EC2 team from Cape Town, South Africa, through its 2006 launch, and spearheaded Amazon’s 2015 acquisition of Annapurna Labs, the Israeli chip designer behind its custom silicon.

Sources indicate that in 2018, DeSantis unveiled Graviton. In June, he told Bloomberg that AWS was in talks to sell its Trainium AI chips to other companies for their own data centers.

Industry observers note that he knows chips, data centers and AI infrastructure at enormous scale. The catch, as John noted: he’s never been a CEO, and the board may want that experience given the circumstances.

According to recent reports, the other Amazon name: Dave Treadwell took over AWS compute and machine learning services in August. Treadwell spent 27 years at Microsoft, where he worked on Windows NT, .NET and Xbox and rose to corporate vice president, before joining Amazon in 2016.

The Microsoft bench: On the podcast, Todd ran through a few Microsoft executives who would bring relevant experience:.

Sources indicate that the insider with Microsoft roots: Nick Parker, a 26-year Microsoft sales veteran, joined Nvidia in August as executive vice president of worldwide field operations, with a pay package worth more than $40 million. He’s newly introduced, but he already runs the team that sells Nvidia’s chips to the world’s largest companies.

One more angle: Whoever gets the job will face a growing list of customers trying to reduce their reliance on Nvidia, including Amazon. In his annual shareholder letter in April, Jassy wrote that Amazon’s chips business would have an annual run rate of about $50 billion if it sold chips to AWS and other third parties the way other chipmakers do.

Jassy noted it’s “quite possible” Amazon will sell racks of them to third parties in the future.

Recent findings suggest that in a Bloomberg interview recorded Oct. 14, Huang said he hoped his successor was already inside the company. The board has said it will consider both internal and external candidates.

CME FedWatch puts the implied chance of a Fed rate hike at 100% for the December 9 meeting, according to the November 12 snapshot. This is another source of pressure on Bitcoin, and there is a good chance the market is going to face its full effect.

Sources indicate that bitcoin and the cryptocurrency market in general aren't set in stone and are highly affected by the performance of traditional markets and the global economy. A rate hike directly affects the desire of investors to expose themselves to riskier assets like crypto.

Bitcoin has been going down rapidly even without the additional source of pressure from the Fed. The current BTC price drop appears to be mostly fueled by insufficient compensation for the risk: Bitcoin and crypto in general aren't as attractive as tech or AI stocks, so it is far better to get exposed to the latter ones.

Recent findings suggest that that is the bearish reading here. FedWatch reflects futures pricing, so the hike is already expected rather than guaranteed to become a fresh shock.

Recent findings suggest that bitcoin is trading at $72,744, below all the moving averages shown on the daily chart. A drop below $70,000 shouldn't necessarily trigger any substantial surge of selling pressure, considering how stretched the decline already looks.

In a recent development, the imbalance of inflows and outflows is still staggering in this reading of the market. The concern is that almost every top-15 crypto asset remains in endurance mode, facing persistent outflows fueled by security concerns, a retreat in investor sentiment and a lack of substantial recovery prospects.

Recent findings suggest that this view draws on Coinglass, CryptoQuant and SosoValue, which track derivatives, on-chain activity and ETF behavior respectively. The interpretation is that all three fields show outflows from digital assets alongside a growing supply of stablecoins.

Industry observers note that A full-blown recovery of the cryptocurrency market would need new catalysts and use cases. A potential burst of the AI bubble, with substantial losses for the largest market players, might push them towards digital assets. A transition is possible, but it's not guaranteed by any means.

The confirmation of a market recovery would only come if we witness higher highs and constant inflows into institutional products like ETFs.

#6095. Latest Update: 8 USDA food safety rules for the 40°F to 140°F danger zone

📅 16 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 14m • 📚 Deep Dive (2828 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Qz ↗ Open Full Page

Latest Update: 8 USDA food safety rules for the 40°F to 140°F danger zone

📅 16 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 14 min read (2828 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Qz

⏱️ ~14 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that food left out more than 2 hours, or 1 hour above 90°F, is risky.
  • It has been revealed that most people decide whether a dish left on the counter is still good by looking at it and giving it a sniff.
  • According to recent reports, the risk reveals up less in the refrigerator than at the long holiday meal or the buffet, where dishes sit out for hours and nobody keeps track of the time.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that food left out more than 2 hours, or 1 hour above 90°F, is risky. Eight USDA rules cover timing, temperatures and handwashing.

It has been revealed that most people decide whether a dish left on the counter is still good by looking at it and giving it a sniff. That check offers no protection against the germs that make people sick, because they grow across the whole range of temperatures between the refrigerator and the oven. A dish that has come out of the oven but has not yet gone into the refrigerator falls somewhere in that range. These bacteria also generally cause no change in how food tastes, smells or looks, according to FSIS. A dish can pass every test a nose or an eye can give it and still make someone ill. The checks that work are the ones made with a clock and a thermometer: how long the food has been out, and how hot or cold it is.

According to recent reports, the risk reveals up less in the refrigerator than at the long holiday meal or the buffet, where dishes sit out for hours and nobody keeps track of the time. Once food reaches the home, keeping it safe becomes the cook's job. "Food safety doesn’t stop at the processing establishments that produce the food you eat," Dr. Mindy Brashears, USDA Under Secretary for Food Safety, said. That job lasts as long as the gathering does, and the CDC advises checking food temperatures regularly throughout an event. Each safeguard is a check that someone has to remember to make. None of them is built into the food.

The Food Safety and Inspection Service, part of the USDA, laid out the federal government's rules for keeping food out of the "danger zone" of 40°F to 140°F. Those rules range from how long a dish can safely sit out to how to reheat leftovers and why clean hands matter. Most of them work the same way. They keep food at one edge of that range or the other, limit how long it spends inside it, or heat it back out. One rule has nothing to do with temperature, because germs also reach food on people's hands, no matter how carefully a cook watches the thermometer. Together, the rules add up to a short set of habits: glancing at the clock, reaching for the thermometer, and stopping at the sink.

Industry observers note that A dish left on the table can become unsafe within the length of an ordinary meal. "Bacteria grow most rapidly in the range of temperatures between 40 °F and 140 °F, doubling in number in as little as 20 minutes," the USDA's Food Safety and Inspection Service said. That is about as long as a conversation over dessert. The phrase "as little as" describes the fastest case, not a rate every dish will follow. A safe habit still has to initiative around that fastest case, because nobody at the table knows how swiftly the germs in their own dish are growing. The growth also builds on itself. Each stretch of time out adds latest germs on top of the ones that grew before it, so a few extra minutes cost more than they seem to.

The fast doubling applies to germs that can make people sick, not only to food that is going stale. That turns a forgotten platter from a question of taste into a question of health.

Recent findings suggest that nobody can watch germs multiply inside a casserole, but a cook can move the dish out of the danger zone by chilling it or heating it. Because the growth compounds, how soon food leaves the zone matters as much as whether it leaves at all.

Every minute a dish spends between 40°F and 140°F counts against it.

The safety check for food on a buffet table is a clock, and food out of the refrigerator has a firm limit of 2 hours, according to the Food Safety and Inspection Service. The USDA sets the same two-hour limit in its latest advice for spring holiday meals. A host will meet that deadline at a weeknight dinner, an office potluck and a holiday table alike. This makes the decision at the table a yes-or-no one. A dish is either within its two hours or past them, and the rule leaves no room for a guess that it is probably still fine. Only a host who noted when the food came out can apply the limit, so the habit starts the moment a dish reaches the table.

The two-hour limit is the general rule, but hot weather shortens it. A host serving food on a day hotter than 90°F has just 1 hour before the food must go back into the cold. A picnic table or a backyard cookout in summer sun often gets that hot without anyone treating the day as unusual, so the stricter limit applies more often than people expect. The USDA advises that eggs meant for eating can stay at room temperature for two hours. Under the hot-weather rule, the same eggs served at a sweltering outdoor spread would have only one hour. Taking the food outside, not anything about the food itself, shortens the deadline, and a host who remembers only "two hours" will go past it.

Anyone serving food outdoors in summer should plan around the shorter of the two limits.

According to recent reports, A cooked dish still needs protecting after the cook turns off the burner, because the rule covers hot food that isn't served right away, the stretch most cooks treat as downtime. The USDA's Food Safety and Inspection Service says that such food should be kept at 140°F or higher, for example with warming equipment. A cook can't count on the heat a pan carries out of the oven, and a casserole cooling under foil on the counter falls short of the rule. The 140°F line is the top edge of the danger zone, and a dish that slips a few degrees below it is back in the range where bacteria grow fastest. The CDC uses the 40°F to 140°F range as the danger zone for Clostridium perfringens, a germ that causes food poisoning. Holding food hot adds no safety to a dish. It keeps a properly cooked dish from losing the safety the cook already gave it.

According to recent reports, meeting the rule takes no specialist gear. Chafing dishes, steam tables that have been preheated, warming trays and slow cookers can all keep food at that temperature, according to the Food Safety and Inspection Service. Once a host hands the job of holding the heat to one of these devices, the device itself needs checking. With a warmer set too low or a thermometer that reads wrong, the food can cool below 140°F while everything on the table looks in order. The CDC advises food service workers to check that their equipment and thermometers work.

A switched-on warming tray is no proof that the food is hot. The proof is a reading from a thermometer someone has checked.

Recent findings suggest that the cold side of a holiday spread looks like the safe side, which makes it easy to forget. A bowl of potato salad or a shrimp platter set on ice seems protected for as long as the meal lasts. A cold dish counts as safe only while its temperature holds at 40°F or colder, and resting it in a bed of ice is one way a host can keep it there, according to the Food Safety and Inspection Service. That temperature is the bottom edge of the danger zone, and a cold dish that warms a few degrees on the table has moved into the range where germs grow. As the meal goes on and the ice melts, the food can warm past that line without any guest noticing.

Industry observers note that A host can also limit how much cold food sits out at once, instead of relying on the ice alone. The USDA advises setting out smaller portions and replenishing them as needed. The less food on the table at a time, the less of it can warm into the zone before guests eat it or the host returns it to the fridge. Cold holding becomes a job that lasts the whole meal, with the host returning to the refrigerator for fresh portions until the last guest is served.

Recent findings suggest that keeping food cold starts days before the meal, with the frozen turkey. The USDA states leaving a turkey out on the counter to thaw is unsafe, and a bird thawing in the refrigerator needs 24 hours for each 4 to 5 pounds of its weight. On the counter, the bird would spend hours well above the 40°F line that the cold rule exists to hold. Safe thawing is therefore a scheduling job as much as a temperature one, and a cook who takes a holiday turkey out of the freezer the night before has already run out of time to thaw it safely.

Cold food stays safe through the calendar and the refill as much as through the ice bucket.

Recent findings suggest that cooking is the step where a cook heats food past the danger zone on purpose, and the rule behind it sets two separate checks. The oven should be no cooler than 325°F, and the meat or poultry itself has to reach a safe internal temperature, according to the Food Safety and Inspection Service. A properly set oven is only the starting condition. The Food Safety and Inspection Service gives 145°F as the target for a roast, chop or steak of beef, pork or lamb. A cook takes that reading from the middle of the meat, and it sits far below the oven setting, so a hot oven tells a cook only that the roast is still cooking. The meat is done when its center reaches the target, not when the oven has been hot for long enough.

A cook who keeps a single "safe" number in mind is following a rule that doesn't exist. The Food Safety and Inspection Service sets ground beef's safe temperature at 160°F, higher than the target for a whole cut, and poultry's at 165°F. A steak and a burger therefore call for different readings, and chicken and turkey need the most heat of the three. Remembering only one number causes trouble either way. A cook who uses the whole-cut figure for everything leaves a burger undercooked, and one who uses the poultry figure for everything dries out a roast. The thermometer has to be read against the right target for the food in hand.

Reaching the target protects the meat only until the cook takes it off the heat. The Food Safety and Inspection Service warns that cooked food should never go back onto the platter that held it raw. A cook who carries burgers back from the grill on the plate that brought them out can put the germs that cooking was meant to kill back onto the finished meat.

Cooking is a job finished at the plate, not at the thermometer reading.

Leftovers get no latest deadline when the meal ends. The Food Safety and Inspection Service indicates cooked food should go into the refrigerator within two hours. A dish's time on the buffet counts toward that limit as much as the minutes it waits after dessert. At a long gathering where guests graze all afternoon, a dish set out at the start can use up its two hours before anyone thinks to pack it away. By the time the last guest leaves, much of the time for clearing the table is already gone.

It has been revealed that getting leftovers into the fridge on time is only part of the job, because cooling them properly matters just as much. "One of the most common causes of foodborne illness is improper cooling of cooked foods," the Food Safety and Inspection Service remarked. The danger lies in the cooling step itself, not only in whether anyone remembers to refrigerate the food. The agency pairs that warning with an instruction to pack leftovers in shallow containers. The choice of container is part of the safety rule rather than a matter of tidiness, so a host has to think about how food goes into the fridge as well as when.

Recent findings suggest that hosts can shrink the leftover job before there are any leftovers. For a game-day spread, FSIS recommends serving the food in smaller batches, one round for each half. With less food sitting out at once, less of it can pass the two-hour limit before cleanup. The host also has less food to cool in a hurry at the end.

A host who decides how much to set out, and when, has settled the size of the leftover job long before anyone clears the plates.

Sources indicate that reheating is the step meant to kill the bacteria in leftovers, not just slow their growth, and its test is a temperature taken inside the food. The Food Safety and Inspection Service says that a dish of leftovers is ready when steam rises from it or when its middle registers 165°F. FSIS advises taking that reading with a food thermometer. The target covers the inside of the food, so a hot oven or a sizzling crust doesn't show that a dish is safe, and a plate too hot to touch can still fall short. The probe belongs at the center, the last part of a dish to get hot.

It has been revealed that steaming is the easier test, and most people will reach for it, but it comes with no number attached. The thermometer reading is the measured standard for leftovers. A cook who goes by steam is still following the guidance, but a cook who uses a thermometer has a firmer answer.

Sources indicate that the bigger trap is a dish that is hot in one spot and cool in another. Federal advice on microwaving aims to heat food evenly, and FSIS recommends checking the temperature in several places. One reading can land on a hot spot and miss a cooler pocket elsewhere in the dish. In practice, the 165°F rule applies to the coolest part of the food, not the first spot the thermometer touches.

In a recent development, liquids get a simpler test that a cook can see in the pot. FSIS states sauces, soups and gravies should be brought to a rolling boil. The reheating check also decides whether food can be saved, because leftovers thawed in the microwave can go back in the freezer once they have been heated to 165°F.

After that last temperature check, the remaining safeguard is the cook's own hands.

Every other safeguard against the danger zone comes down to a reading on a clock or a thermometer. Handwashing comes down to whether a cook stops at the sink at all. Washing with soap and warm water for at least 20 seconds helps get germs off a cook's hands, according to the Food Safety and Inspection Service. A wash that takes well under a minute and no special equipment is easy to do and just as easy to skip. Much of the risk lies in the washes that never happen.

Skipping the wash is a serious lapse, because hands are how food workers usually contaminate food. In outbreaks traced to food that restaurant workers contaminated, the workers had spread germs from their hands to the food in nine of ten, according to the CDC. The short scrub the USDA recommends is the step meant to block that route. The moment that matters is when a cook moves from raw meat to the next task without stopping at the sink.

According to recent reports, even in restaurant kitchens, where handling food is the job, most of the washes that should happen don't. Restaurant workers do about nine tasks an hour that should send them to the sink, the CDC reports, but they wash only about two or three times an hour. Handwashing is meant to interrupt cooking again and again through every hour, and in a busy kitchen that interruption is the first thing to go.

It has been revealed that conditions in the kitchen, not a stricter rule, get people washing more. The CDC finds that restaurant workers wash more often during slower stretches, at restaurants that train their staff in food safety, and in kitchens with several hand sinks or a sink in plain view. Those conditions make the USDA's 20-second instruction easier to follow. Anyone feeding a crowd at home can apply the same lesson by clearing the sink, setting out soap and putting both where people can see them.

Clean hands depend as much on where the sink is as on anyone's willpower.

At KubeCon 2026, the illusion of AI control meets the reality of implementation

📅 16 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 12 min read (2315 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Siliconangle

⏱️ ~12 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • GUEST COLUMN by Jason English.
  • I revisited Salt Lake City for KubeCon/CloudNativeCon NA 2026 hoping to find practical approaches to delivering customer value amidst a rapidly shifting kaleidoscope of artificial intelligence-driven solutions that are making it increasingly difficult to trust our own eyes and ears.
  • This year, the host Cloud Native Computing Foundation set its theme as “Cloud Native Without Limits,” and judging by the record-shattering pace of latest community developments with more than 230 active projects, and the increasing adoption rate of AI for building and consuming applications, the momentum will only grow.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

UPDATED 11:41 EST / NOVEMBER 16 2026.

GUEST COLUMN by Jason English.

I revisited Salt Lake City for KubeCon/CloudNativeCon NA 2026 hoping to find practical approaches to delivering customer value amidst a rapidly shifting kaleidoscope of artificial intelligence-driven solutions that are making it increasingly difficult to trust our own eyes and ears.

This year, the host Cloud Native Computing Foundation set its theme as “Cloud Native Without Limits,” and judging by the record-shattering pace of latest community developments with more than 230 active projects, and the increasing adoption rate of AI for building and consuming applications, the momentum will only grow.

“If you look back at last year’s KubeCon in Atlanta, OpenClaw was not released yet, MCP was less than a year old, and inference in cloud native was just getting started,” Chris Anzyzcyk, chief technical officer of CNCF, said in the opening remarks.

Recent findings suggest that “We knew we were moving out of a phase where most of the AI compute was used for training and we were going to massively ramp up inference,” stated Jonathan Bryce, executive director of CNCF. “Just in the last eight months, we’ve seen a 4X increase in inference traffic across the industry. That’s really an incredible increase in the AI footprint. Inference is no longer just an opportunity, it’s now a cloud-native production workload.”.

With more than 350K CNCF contributors and 21.2 million cloud-native developers worldwide, fully three-quarters of them are already using AI coding agents, according to the latest State of Cloud Native Development Q3 2026 report, and a show of hands in the room hinted at a much higher presence of AI tooling on the engineer’s desktop.

Likewise, two-thirds of self-described AI-driven organizations are standardizing on Kubernetes and related open-source technologies.

Sources indicate that there’s a clear connection here, but AI is not the whole story. Enterprises still need to modernize their application fleets, and deploy, scale, secure and observe their most critical systems, in order to get beyond the AI hype and realize business value.

With an open mind and a skeptical eye, here were some of the interesting newly introduced perspectives and vendor solutions I encountered at the show.

With the rapid enterprise rollout of agentic AI, every developer is being challenged to apply human decision insight while working at agent speed, one of the major themes of the show.

Getting there will take more than new technologies, it will also require a lot of collaboration and understanding. The Kubernetes AI Conformance Program released at KubeCon NA 2025 now has 42 major participating vendors agreeing to consistent standards, and this year there are new Kubernetes AI Certifications for upskilling engineers, whether they are just starting out, or if they are “Golden Kubestronauts” who already passed every course CNCF offers.

“Kubernetes has become the standard API for deploying a workload to a computer, including AI,” remarked Dan Ciruli, vice president and general manager for cloud native at Nutanix Inc. “The reason, in my opinion, is because the CNCF gave a safe haven for anyone from the smallest startup of two people to the largest companies on Earth to feel safe in donating labor, and code, and IP, and agreeing on things. And that, in turn, gave everybody, from governments to financial services to hot startups, the confidence that they could consume it.”.

The firm recently introduced their Nutanix Agent Gateway and an NKP Metal solution that allows Kubernetes clusters and workloads to run on bare metal as well as virtual machines in EKS, AKS or GKE for what they call a “dual-native” experience.

“How are you going to safely and sustainably connect thousands of agents to the systems of record that actually run the business such as customer loyalty or inventory?” asked Matt DeBergalis, CEO, Apollo Graph Inc., doing business as Apollo GraphQL, which supports the popular open source GraphQL query language, presenting a fresh semantic domain model for deterministically interpreting AI prompts and controls for each record.

Last year CNCF announced a Dynamic Resource Allocation or DRA capability, which unlocked fresh possibilities for the community to optimize AI workloads running in Kubernetes. This year, sandboxing, or running agents in secure instances to prevent escapes, hijacking and overprovisioning, was the watchword.

Development has moved fast in this area, with two upcoming projects: a Agent Substrate layer contributed by Google that optimizes resource consumption of thousands of agent sandboxes, and OpenShell, an Nvidia Corp.-contributed project for secure sandboxed runtimes.

Startup Apelogic Inc. doing business as HyperShell built an operational agent envelope based on OpenShell that defines guardrails what systems an autonomous agent can access, and what actions it can take, based on the business or system intent the agent was intended to serve.

In a recent development, cast AI started out as a cloud cost optimization layer for rightsizing clusters on major hyperscalers, but as cloud native infrastructure started taking over enterprise environments, it now finds itself automating and optimizing more AI workloads across CPUs and GPUs, memory and storage. New at KubeCon, their Kimchi code agent governs and deploys application infrastructures from a prompt, which allows developers shift left agentic reviews before production tuning.

According to recent reports, floxdev Inc., which I covered as a startup with their Nix-based lean containerized environment deployments in 2025, put its Flox platform directly in the AI delivery path, giving agents skills to stamp out identical complete environments that include all dependencies, without reproducing any element of the software supply chain inventory that wasn’t intended to change. This moves agentic loops faster with lower compute costs, but the real value is when human engineers can reduce future maintenance and security remediation costs.

This year’s CNCF graduation of the OpenTelemetry project couldn’t come at a better moment, making OTel the lingua franca of application performance, scalability and reliability.

While observability was traditionally considered the domain of engineers and operators, now everyone from data analysts to business executives may be using an LLM or an agent to interact with enterprise applications, potentially changing software, or delivering more agents, in the process.

In a recent development, splunk, a division of Cisco Systems Inc. has added to its agent observability suite with a specialized language model called Eval-G1 that can run prompt-and-response evals in sub-second times at sub-cent costs, giving engineers the ability to interrupt a faulty response in real time, before it reaches customers. A upcoming Evaluation Studio helps teams generate guardrails in a low-code graphical environment. Also cool, a tokenomics feature (from the recent acquisition of Galileo, which we just covered) that analyzes token spend versus system and business performance metrics.

“It’s been exciting to see how OpenTelemetry, which started out as tens of thousands of adaptors for every application and client, has transitioned with the AI revolution so that now, we have frameworks that just emit OTel natively,” said Morgan McLean, senior director of product management at Splunk and OpenTelemetry co-creator. “So Splunk, and our competitors, can just launch new observability features without putting 30 people on writing new integrations.”.

Recent findings suggest that since a lot of AI projects start out as experiments, observability stalwart Dynatrace LLC has made several moves to meet smaller teams where they are in validating each feature for performance and reliability before enterprise-scale rollouts. It recently acquired Bindplane for OTel-native telemetry pipelines, BlueBox, which gives developers a custom agent for debugging and checks within a coding IDE, and Arize, which maintains the popular Phoenix open-source tool for AI evaluations.

New Relic Inc. released a new Autopilot Kubernetes Agent, a virtual SRE that users can interact with via natural language to look across telemetry and APM data to assess the health of the cluster and application, triage issues with a complete stack trace, and recommend resolutions.

“Especially when you bring agents into your environment, you can’t just take your telemetry and throw it over to a general-purpose LLM, because there are known deterministic patterns and historical insights about Kubernetes we’ve been working to resolve for years,” said Jemiah Sius, vice president of market strategy and developer relations at Fresh Relic.

A lot of the governance difficulty with agents and sandboxes and policies isn’t a technical problem; it is about user experience. Human engineers don’t like being “in the loop” for AI, aka “Meat Proxies,” that continuously pass along approvals. Humans need to be in control, with less toil and more focus on what customers want out of AI applications.

Recent findings suggest that “You can try to create a secure agent sandbox with a policy where everything is disabled by default until a human approves it, but eventually, someone gets tired of being in that approval loop,” stated Simone Morellato, senior director of product marketing, Rafay Systems Inc., an AI infrastructure delivery platform used by leading neoclouds. “So you give an agent access to one thing, and eventually you end up giving them access to everything. And at that point, you are back at square one.”.

Since I covered Edera Inc. last year, this hardened runtime container vendor is finding latest traction in this agentic age by continuing to strengthen the stack from the bottom up, with an agent runtime and OCAP bounded authority that acts as a switchboard for discretely defined agent capabilities, rather than assigning agents credentials or access to MCP servers or APIs or other agents that can be expanded or exploited for another HuggingFace-type incident.

Sources indicate that “You can consume capabilities in our system and publish capabilities,” said Edera founder and Chief Technology Officer Alex Zenla. So, for example, for an MCP server, we publish each tool call as a capability. And then when you spin up your agent, you ask for the tool calls that you want. And then it consumes just those capabilities. And we’re able to enforce policies because we have one central pathway for everything to go through, so we can know exactly which agents are using which capabilities.”.

“I love the focus on reliability that I’ve seen in the talks and on the floor here at KubeCon,” stated Kolton Andrus, CEO of Gremlin Inc., which was there demonstrating their latest Foresight AI solution that proactively injects failure conditions in order to identify and remediate failure risks. “You can no longer wait for things to fall apart before taking action. “Everyone’s moving 100 miles an hour trying to keep up with AI, and waking up to the fact that reliability can’t be an afterthought anymore. You can no longer wait for things to fall apart before taking action.”.

According to recent reports, this being my eighth KubeCon, I keep coming back because the community atmosphere here is unparalleled. There’s a real sense of camaraderie among developers and engineers from wildly different backgrounds, as they build upcoming fundamentals and enjoy the journey toward a cloud native future.

According to recent reports, we’ve come a long way over the last eleven years since Kubernetes was introduced. Interoperability, portability, control planes, observability, networking, identity, security and many more mature capabilities are there for the taking. Now AI is being layered on top. But that’s not the story here.

In a recent development, what really impresses me is how much this open source community gives back for the benefit of everyone. All of these people have real jobs to do, and yet they invest their own time, as much as the software industry invests in them.

Indeed, as CNCF’s own Jonathan Bryce said: “Some problems can only be solved in the open.”.

Industry News: XRP Risks Losing $1 Amid Aggressive $2.5 Billion Shift

💡 Key Takeaways
  • As XRP continues to struggle amid the broad crypto market volatility while failing in multiple attempts to recover, key on-chain metrics are pointing to increased selling pressure among traders.
  • While momentum remains extremely weak, latest data from crypto analytics platform, Cryptoquant, highlights that sellers have dominated both XRP’s spot and futures markets, putting it at risk of losing the long-held $1 mark.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

As XRP continues to struggle amid the broad crypto market volatility while failing in multiple attempts to recover, key on-chain metrics are pointing to increased selling pressure among traders.

While momentum remains extremely weak, latest data from crypto analytics platform, Cryptoquant, highlights that sellers have dominated both XRP’s spot and futures markets, putting it at risk of losing the long-held $1 mark.

Per the data, XRP’s cumulative volume delta (CVD) across major cryptocurrency exchanges shows that aggressive selling has dominated both its spot and futures market since September 23.

According to recent reports, as of November 12, XRP’s Perpetual CVD on Binance has fallen from -$109 million to about -$1.1 billion. It is notable to note that the CVD of an asset is a key metric that measures the difference between the volume of aggressive buy orders and aggressive sell orders over time.

While the metric turns negative when more traders are aggressively selling than buying, the -991 million negative balance in the Binance perpetual CVD signals stronger selling pressure.

With the negative balance on Binance exceeding its previous level by more than 10 times, this demonstrates that traders have placed significantly more market sell orders than buy orders, either by opening short positions or closing existing long positions.

Apart from its futures market, further data reveals that sellers have also dominated XRP’s spot activity across all major crypto exchanges, including Binance.

Notably, XRP’s All CEX Estimated Spot CVD moved from -$400 million to -$2.9 billion over the same period.

While this marks a $2.5 billion increase in the imbalance favoring sellers, it indicates that XRP spot traders have also been selling XRP more aggressively rather than buying, propelling the asset for further price declines.

11 federal holidays in 2027, and 9 of them give a three-day weekend

Recent findings suggest that OPM's 2027 schedule lists 11 federal holidays. See each date, which ones create a three-day weekend, and which observed days shift.

Industry observers note that A federal holiday becomes a three-day weekend only when it sits beside a Saturday or a Sunday, and the law settles that in two very different ways. The National Park Service reports that a rule tied to a day of the week sets Martin Luther King Jr. Day, which means the holiday lands on a different date every year. FSIS reports that federal law fixes New Year's Day to a calendar date. That holiday's weekday, and with it the day off, shifts from one year to the next. Holidays tied to a weekday can promise a long weekend years in advance. For holidays tied to a date, the long weekend depends on which weekday the date falls on, and 2027 is an unusually good year for them. Every holiday except Veterans Day and Thanksgiving, which both fall on Thursdays, ends up as a Friday or a Monday off.

Industry observers note that A holiday that falls on a weekend is not lost, because for most federal workers the day off moves into the workweek, right beside the weekend. FSIS reports that when a holiday lands on a Saturday, a worker whose week runs Monday through Friday takes the Friday before it off, while a worker whose week runs Tuesday through Saturday and has a holiday land on Sunday takes the Tuesday after it. The same holiday can produce a different day off for workers on different schedules. Part-time employees are not entitled to a substitute holiday at all, so when a holiday falls on their regular day off, no other day replaces it. A long weekend on the federal calendar is a promise made to the standard full-time schedule, and anyone on a different schedule needs to check how the rules apply to them.

Sources indicate that the U.S. Office of Personnel Management set out to show the official 2027 federal holiday dates for federal employees, from Juneteenth to Columbus Day to Veterans Day. Those dates are the government's own record for its workforce and the baseline for checking any other schedule. The date written into law and the day off are not always the same, and the observed date is the one to proposal around. For most employees, a holiday that falls on a Sunday is observed the following Monday. Each holiday raises the same two questions: whether it brings a three-day weekend, and what else the day carries in 2027.

Federal workers start 2027 with a three-day weekend that no weekend-shift rule had to create. New Year's Day is tied by federal law to January 1, according to FSIS, so the holiday keeps its date no matter which weekday that date turns out to be. The U.S. Office of Personnel Management lists the 2027 holiday on Friday, January 1, with no shifted observance attached. Employees on a standard Monday-to-Friday schedule therefore get Friday through Sunday off. For them, the date in the law and the day off are the same day this time, and there is no substitute day to look up. That match does not hold every year, and the two separate again before 2027 is over.

According to recent reports, anyone planning the end of 2027 should count a second Latest Year's day off, one that belongs to 2028 but is taken in December. New Year's Day 2028 is a Saturday, so federal employees observe it on Friday, December 31, 2027. Calendar year 2027 therefore holds two New Year's holidays, both on Fridays. A standard federal worker gets two three-day weekends out of them, one in the first days of the year and one in its last. Travel, family visits or a quiet stretch at home can be planned around either, as long as the second one goes on the right day of the calendar.

For the turn of 2028, put the day off on December 31, not on January 1.

Industry observers note that federal workers can count on a three-day weekend for the Birthday of Martin Luther King, Jr. every year, because the holiday is always on a Monday. In 2027 it falls on Monday, January 18, according to the U.S. Office of Personnel Management. That is the holiday's own date and not a substitute day moved from a weekend, and federal staff have Saturday, January 16, through Monday off. The weekday stays fixed while the date moves. The holiday was on Monday, January 19, in 2026 and will be on Monday, January 17, in 2028. Anyone who prepares a trip around the 2026 date will book the wrong weekend, so the date has to come from the 2027 calendar.

Sources indicate that king's family meant the holiday as a day of service to others, not a day of rest. "The greatest birthday gift my husband could receive is if people of all racial and ethnic backgrounds celebrated the holiday by performing individual acts of kindness through service to others," Coretta Scott King, Dr. King's wife, said, as reported by the National Park Service. By her measure, the Monday is a day to help someone, and a free day is only part of what it offers. Because the time off is settled in advance, the question for federal workers is what the extra day is for.

In a recent development, three days off give people enough time to visit the places where King's work happened. Those places include the Martin Luther King, Jr. National Historical Park in Georgia, the Birmingham Civil Rights National Monument in Alabama, and the Martin Luther King Jr. Memorial in Washington, according to the National Park Service. A visit to any of them ties the long weekend to the person the holiday honors.

Federal workers never need a lucky calendar for this long weekend, and the only choice they have to make is how to spend it.

Industry observers note that the law places Washington's Birthday on a Monday, so federal workers get a February long weekend without having to check which weekday the holiday falls on. The holiday's official designation is the third Monday of February, the National Weather Service reports, and in 2027 that day is Monday, February 15, according to the U.S. Office of Personnel Management. The three-day weekend comes from the rule itself rather than from a lucky year on the calendar. Readers need to look up only the date each year, never the weekday.

With the weekday fixed, the holiday's date changes each year and never matches Washington's actual birthday. In 2028 the holiday falls on Monday, February 21, which is the latest date the holiday can fall on, according to the National Weather Service. Washington was born on February 22, one day after that latest date, so the observed Monday cannot fall on his real birthday in any year. Anyone planning around the holiday should mark the Monday on the calendar, not February 22.

Industry observers note that the holiday most people call Presidents Day appears on the federal schedule under its legal name, Washington's Birthday. That name is set out in Title 5 of the U.S. Code, Section 6103(a), according to the National Weather Service. The Office of Personnel Management and the weather service both make it a rule to use the name in the law, even where a state, a city or a company prefers another name for the day. The different name on the federal calendar is a deliberate choice, not a missing holiday.

A store sign may say Presidents Day and the federal calendar may say Washington's Birthday, but federal workers get the same Monday off.

Memorial Day gives federal workers a three-day weekend every year, because the law ties the holiday to a Monday rather than to a date. The days off are certain, but the date moves within the last week of May, and in 2027 the holiday comes as late in the month as it can. It falls on the last day of May, Monday, May 31, according to the U.S. Office of Personnel Management. The Federal Reserve Board lists the 2026 holiday on May 25, almost a week earlier, so anyone who reuses the 2026 date in a 2027 plan will book a trip or a rental for the wrong week. In 2027 the break runs from Saturday, May 29, through the holiday Monday. Planners also have no substitute day to find this year. The Monday shown on the federal schedule is the day off, and no weekend shift applies to the holiday on the Federal Reserve's own schedule either.

The guaranteed Monday had a cost, because the holiday gave up a date of its own to become one. Before the change, Memorial Day was fixed on May 30, according to the National Weather Service. In 2027 May 30 is the Sunday just before the Monday holiday, so the traditional date falls inside the three-day weekend. People who mark the day on May 30 itself don't have to choose this year between the original date and a long weekend away. A standard Monday-to-Friday federal worker gets both.

In 2027, the original Memorial Day and the federal day off fall on the same weekend.

Industry observers note that federal workers get a long weekend for Juneteenth in 2027 only because the holiday's legal date falls on a Saturday. Federal employees observe the holiday on Friday, June 18, because June 19 is a Saturday in 2027, according to the U.S. Office of Personnel Management. The Friday off sits next to the weekend and gives them a Friday-to-Sunday break. If June 19 fell in the middle of the week, the same holiday would bring no long weekend at all.

Juneteenth will not move to a dependable Monday, because its date marks a specific day in history. The U.S. Census Bureau reports that General Order No. 3 was issued in Galveston, Texas, on June 19, 1865. "The people of Texas are informed that in accordance with a Proclamation from the Executive of the United States, all slaves are free," Major General Gordon Granger's order mentioned. The holiday keeps the day of that announcement, whatever the weekday. That gives Juneteenth more weight than a convenient Monday would. It also means federal workers get a long weekend only in years when June 19 falls on or next to a weekend.

The 2027 day off falls on the same date as the first Juneteenth federal holiday. The U.S. Census Bureau reports that the Juneteenth federal holiday was signed into law on June 17, 2021. The first observed holiday came a day later, on Friday, June 18, 2021, and federal employees get that same Friday date off in 2027. The tradition goes back to 1865, but the federal day off is only a few years old.

According to recent reports, outside the federal workforce, a Juneteenth day off is less certain. Juneteenth has official standing in all 50 states and in the District of Columbia, according to the U.S. Census Bureau, but that standing can be an observance rather than a state holiday. An observance recognizes the day without guaranteeing anyone a day off work. Before planning a three-day trip, workers outside the federal government should check whether their state or employer closes on Friday, June 18.

According to recent reports, independence Day gives federal workers a three-day weekend in 2027, with the holiday itself in the middle of it. July 4 is a Sunday this year, so people celebrate on a day most of them already have off rather than on a workday. Federal employees still get a day off for the holiday, on Monday, July 5, according to the U.S. Office of Personnel Management. Their break runs from Saturday through Monday, and the Fourth is the second of those three days. Anyone who stays out late for fireworks on Sunday night still has a full free day before going back to work on Tuesday.

Anyone who repeats last summer's prepares will find the extra day on the other side of the holiday. In 2026, federal employees observed Independence Day on Friday, July 3, so their extra day came before the Fourth rather than after it. Workers get the same number of days off in both years, but a trip takes a different shape. A 2026 getaway could start on Friday morning, while a 2027 trip starts on Saturday and leaves Monday for the trip home. Travelers $TRV who book a rental for the same nights as last year would arrive a day before their time off begins and check out before it ends.

In 2027, the nation's birthday comes with a day off after it.

Sources indicate that labor Day gives federal workers a three-day weekend in 2027 without help from the calendar or from any weekend-shift rule. The holiday falls on Monday, Sept. 6, 2027, according to the U.S. Office of Personnel Management. Standard Monday-to-Friday federal employees therefore get Saturday through Monday off, and nothing has to be moved to make that happen. A holiday that is always observed on a Monday can never fall midweek or on a weekend, so its long weekend is certain every year. That makes Labor Day one of the surest long weekends to proposal around in 2027.

It has been revealed that the Monday is fixed, but the date is not, and a person who aims from habit can book the wrong weekend. Labor Day in 2026 is Monday, Sept. 7. Anyone who copies that date into a 2027 calendar plans around the day after the holiday, when the long weekend is already over. The date changes again after 2027, when the holiday falls on Monday, Sept. 4, 2028. A date that is right for one year is wrong for the next, so readers will find the long weekend on a different date in the first week of September each year.

The day off itself is never in doubt; the one thing to check each year is which Monday it is.

Columbus Day gives federal workers an autumn long weekend that never depends on luck. Under federal law, the holiday falls on the second Monday of October, according to the National Weather Service. The U.S. Office of Personnel Management lists Monday, Oct. 11, as the 2027 holiday, with no shifted observance attached. The date on the schedule is the day off itself, and no weekend rule has to move it. Federal workers can treat the Saturday-to-Monday break as settled and proposal a trip around it now.

Fixing Columbus Day to a Monday cost the holiday its anniversary. Before the change, the holiday was observed on Oct. 12 every year, according to the National Weather Service. Federal workers now get that anniversary off only in years when Oct. 12 is the second Monday, as it is in 2026, and in 2028 the holiday is Monday, Oct. 9. The 2027 date is good for 2027 only, so anyone booking travel for this weekend in a later year needs to look up that year's second Monday instead of reusing this one.

People argue about what Columbus Day honors, but the dispute has never been about whether federal workers get the day off. In a 2025 Truth Social post, President Donald Trump promised to restore the holiday, and his pledge described the rule that was already in force. "I am hereby reinstating Columbus Day under the same rules, dates, and locations, as it has had for all of the many decades before!" Trump said, as reported by TIME. Congress has not removed Columbus Day from the federal holidays, so the pledge brought back nothing that had been taken away. Congress has also never given Indigenous Peoples Day federal holiday status, even though former President Joe Biden recognized it on the same Monday as Columbus Day. The name a president favors is a political choice, while the law keeps the Monday off in place.

Recent findings suggest that whatever people call it, the 2027 day off is Monday, Oct. 11, and nothing in the naming fight has changed that.

Sources indicate that veterans Day gives federal workers a single midweek day off in 2027, not a three-day weekend. The holiday is tied to the date of Nov. 11 rather than to a weekday, and in 2027 that date is a Thursday, according to the U.S. Office of Personnel Management. The weekend-shift rules apply only to holidays on a Saturday or Sunday, so a Thursday holiday stays where it is. A federal worker gets the day free and then goes back to work on Friday before the weekend begins.

Federal workers get a long weekend for the holiday again a year later. In 2028, Nov. 11 is a Saturday, and federal employees take Friday, Nov. 10, as the observed holiday, with three days off in a row. Veterans Day's weekday changes from one year to the next, so a midweek holiday in one year can turn into a long weekend in the next. Anyone hoping for a long November weekend around Veterans Day should look to 2028.

Veterans Day began as Armistice Day, the Census Bureau reports, and the veterans it honors today come from two very different generations. Post-9/11 veterans were the largest group in 2025, at 31.4% of all veterans. Those who had reached age 75 or older made up nearly as massive a share that year, at 30.5%. The day is about recent wars as much as old ones, and Americans who mark it honor an elderly generation alongside a much younger one.

According to recent reports, A midweek Thursday is a fitting date for a day with that weight. It is a day to mark, not a break to initiative around.

According to recent reports, thanksgiving always falls on a Thursday, so it gives federal workers a holiday but never a long weekend on its own. In 2027 the day off is Thursday, November 25, according to the U.S. Office of Personnel Management. That leaves one ordinary weekday, Friday, between the holiday and the weekend. A Thursday holiday can never land on a Saturday or a Sunday, so the rules that move a weekend holiday into the workweek never apply to it. The date on the schedule is the day off, and nothing about it moves closer to the weekend. On the federal calendar, Thanksgiving stands alone as a Thursday holiday.

The weekday stays the same every year, while the date changes. Thanksgiving falls on Thursday, November 26, in 2026 and on Thursday, November 23, in 2028. A family can blueprint the shape of the break years ahead, even though it has to look up the date each time. Every Thanksgiving trip or gathering starts from a Thursday holiday, never from a Friday or a Monday, and the federal government gives one day off for it. The Friday after Thanksgiving is not a federal holiday. Anyone who wants four days in a row has to arrange that Friday separately, with annual leave or with an employer's own schedule.

For Thanksgiving, readers have to build the long weekend themselves.

Federal workers get a three-day weekend for Christmas in 2027, but their paid day off is Christmas Eve, not Christmas Day. Christmas is on a Saturday this year, so the U.S. Office of Personnel Management lists Friday, Dec. 24, as the observed holiday for federal employees. The year's last federal holiday therefore comes with a break that runs from Christmas Eve through Sunday, and Christmas itself falls in the middle of it rather than at its start. Federal workers who usually spend Dec. 24 at their desks and wrap up last errands after work can treat that Friday as a full free day this year. Anyone who intends around a federal schedule in 2027 should mark Dec. 24 as the day off, not Dec. 25.

A long Christmas weekend is common in the years around 2027, and what changes from year to year is which day federal workers actually get off. In 2026, Christmas is on Friday, Dec. 25, so the long weekend begins on the holiday itself and no day needs to move. In 2028, Christmas is on Monday, Dec. 25, so the holiday ends a long weekend rather than starting one, and the day off and the holiday are again the same day. Of those three years, 2027 is the only one in which the paid day off and Christmas are different days. In 2027, someone who keeps the habit from those other years and marks Dec. 25 as the day off will put it on a Saturday, when federal offices are already closed.

Even the most familiar date on the federal calendar is worth checking for its observed day before anyone books travel or sets a family gathering.

F2Pool co-founder Chun Wang, known on X as Satofishi, bought 5,246 ETH worth $10.78 million over the past two days at an average price of $2,054, according to Lookonchain and Arkham data.

It has been revealed that on Nov. 5, with ether trading near $2,400, Wang sold 6,200 wrapped staked ETH (wstETH) for $18.5 million in USDC. Wrapped staked ETH is a version of Lido's staked ether (stETH) that can be used in DeFi protocols.

This week, ether traded about 14% lower than on the day of the sale, and Wang started buying it back.

He withdrew 5,246 ETH from Binance hot wallets in two transfers of 3,996 ETH and 1,250 ETH. The purchase cost him $10.78 million, so about $7.7 million from the Nov. 5 sale is still left in USDC, according to Lookonchain.

Sources indicate that wang then sent 3,996 ETH ($8.23 million) to Lido. Lido is the largest liquid staking protocol on Ethereum. He deposited the wstETH he received into Spark, a lending protocol in the Sky ecosystem, which was previously known as MakerDAO. In Spark, wstETH can be used as collateral, while it continues to earn staking rewards.

In a recent development, he started out arbitraging Bitcoin between overseas exchanges and China's Taobao and later co-founded F2Pool. He launched the pool in 2013 together with Mao Shixing. At that time, F2Pool was one of the first Bitcoin mining pools in China.

In a recent development, in 2015, he bought a condo in Pattaya for 2,900 BTC. He later sold it for 7 BTC, as the price of Bitcoin had risen many times over.

In 2025, Wang also funded and commanded Fram2, the first crewed spaceflight over Earth's polar regions, on a SpaceX Crew Dragon.

Recent findings suggest that F2Pool also mined ether until Ethereum moved to proof-of-stake in September 2022. Before that, Wang launched the non-custodial staking service stakefish. According to Wang, he decided to do it after a conversation with Vitalik Buterin in 2017. Stakefish was also one of the first node operators of Lido.

Sources indicate that ether is down more than 15% since the start of the month amid outflows from spot ETFs, according to SoSoValue. At press time, ETH is trading at $2,020.
